Volumio Primo Plus

Volumio's Primo Plus is an all-in-one streaming DAC that combines the company's Rivo Plus streaming platform with a DAC section based on the highly regarded Preciso. It runs Volumio's premium OS and is essentially designed for people who want a serious network streamer and DAC without having to buy and connect two separate boxes.

The Primo Plus costs €1,199 and includes a lifetime subscription to Volumio Premium.
What is the Primo Plus?

The original Primo was Volumio's first attempt at combining streaming and DAC functionality in one compact enclosure. The Primo Plus takes that concept considerably further.

The DAC section uses two ESS ES9039Q2M chips in a dual-mono configuration, together with upgraded op-amps, a very low-phase-noise 90fs clock and a dual linear power supply with separate regulation for the analogue and digital sections. The power supply also uses extensive LC filtering and multiple low-value capacitors to keep ESR low.

The streaming side is based on a quad-core Cortex-A72 processor with 2GB of RAM and 16GB of storage, which is more than enough for the relatively lightweight Volumio operating system.

Connectivity is another strong point. You get USB-C for connecting a computer or mobile device, optical and coaxial digital inputs, USB-A for external storage and digital output, Gigabit Ethernet, dual-band Wi-Fi and Bluetooth 5.0.

For analogue output there are both RCA and balanced XLR connectors. The Primo Plus can also work as a preamplifier, with eight selectable output levels ranging from 0.5Vrms to 3.15Vrms through RCA and from 1Vrms to 6.30Vrms through XLR.

In other words, this is considerably more versatile than its small size might suggest.
Non Audio Stuff

The Primo Plus follows Volumio's minimalist design philosophy and looks almost identical to the Preciso. It is a very compact device, measuring just 27 x 15 x 5cm, with a nicely finished aluminium chassis.

There is no huge touchscreen, album-art display or elaborate user interface. Instead, you get a small 1.3-inch OLED screen and two multifunction rotary controls.

The left knob handles power/standby and input selection, while the right one controls volume, mute and DAC filter selection. An included remote control provides another way of operating the unit, while most of the more advanced settings are accessed through the Volumio application.

Personally, I like this approach. I don't really need a large display on a network streamer because my tablet or phone is already a much better interface for browsing music.

The initial setup is straightforward, and the Volumio application is available for Android, iOS and through a web interface. It also provides access to a surprisingly large number of hardware and software settings, including display brightness, power-saving functions, output selection, DAC filters, NOS mode and various levels of output voltage.

The streaming platform supports local playback, AirPlay, Tidal and Tidal Connect, Qobuz and Qobuz Connect, as well as UPnP/DLNA and OpenHome. There are also plugins for services such as Spotify, Roon Bridge, Squeezelite, SoundCloud and others.

One notable omission is Spotify Lossless support.
Audio Stuff

I used the Primo Plus exclusively with its internal streamer, since this is really the main reason to choose an all-in-one device like this. Otherwise, you could simply buy the Preciso DAC and pair it with a Rivo Plus.

I listened to the Primo Plus through my main speaker system as well as with headphones and a dedicated headphone amplifier.

The first thing that becomes obvious is how clean and transparent this DAC sounds.

The Primo Plus is extremely neutral and technically accomplished, with excellent resolution, separation and overall fidelity. At the same time, it avoids the sterile or overly clinical character that can sometimes accompany very transparent ESS-based DACs.

That balance is probably its greatest strength.

The bass is extended, controlled and very well defined, with excellent timing. It isn't particularly heavy or visceral, nor does it have the thickest low-end presentation I've heard, but it never sounds thin or anaemic. There is enough punch and impact to keep things engaging.

The midrange is similarly neutral and precise, with excellent clarity and articulation. It doesn't have an especially rich or harmonically saturated character, and it isn't the most organic-sounding DAC around, but voices and instruments still sound natural and convincing.

The treble is fast, energetic and very resolving. Despite being quite brilliant, it avoids becoming harsh or excessively bright. There is a small amount of the typical digital character that you can associate with highly resolving D/S DACs, but Volumio has done a good job of keeping it under control.

Detail retrieval is excellent without turning the Primo Plus into a piece of studio monitoring equipment. It gives you plenty of information, but doesn't constantly throw details at your face.

The soundstage is another highlight. It is wide and spacious, with very good separation and precise imaging. Both with headphones and speakers in particular, the Primo Plus can produce an impressively open presentation.

It isn't the most holographic or harmonically rich DAC I've heard, and some more sophisticated designs can produce a more atmospheric and organic presentation. Nevertheless, the Primo Plus gets the important things right: it combines high technical performance with enough musicality to remain enjoyable.

And that's ultimately what I like about its sound. You don't listen to it because it has impressive measurements; you listen to it because it sounds good.
NOS mode

One of the most interesting features is the NOS mode.

With the regular oversampling filters, the Primo Plus has the cleaner, more precise and technically impressive presentation you'd expect. Switching to NOS changes the character slightly.

The sound becomes smoother, more relaxed and somewhat more organic, with less of the subtle digital glare I can hear in the standard OS mode. The trade-off is a very small reduction in transparency and technical precision.

For me, NOS is therefore more than just a gimmick. It gives the Primo Plus a genuinely different presentation and makes it more versatile. Listeners who prefer a slightly more relaxed and analogue-like sound will probably enjoy it.
Primo Plus vs Preciso + Rivo Plus

This is probably the most interesting question for anyone already considering Volumio's separate components.

Since the DAC section of the Primo Plus is essentially the same as the Preciso, I wasn't surprised that I couldn't hear any major differences between them.

The separate Preciso and Rivo Plus combination does sound slightly cleaner and more transparent to my ears, with perhaps a little more realism and refinement when playing demanding material. But we're talking about relatively small differences.

The important thing is that the Primo Plus gets extremely close while also giving you the convenience of having everything in one compact box.

Considering that the separate combination costs considerably more, the Primo Plus makes a lot of sense. Unless you have a very revealing high-end system and are prepared to pay considerably more for those last few percent, I'd happily take the Primo Plus and spend the difference elsewhere.
Volumio Lineo5

One optional upgrade worth mentioning is Volumio's Lineo5 linear power supply.

The Primo Plus already has an internal dual linear power supply, but the supplied external switching adapter still feeds it. The Lineo5 replaces that adapter with a 5V/5A linear supply based around a large 120W toroidal transformer and extensive filtering.

The improvement isn't dramatic or transformative, and anyone expecting a night-and-day difference will probably be disappointed. What you get instead are relatively subtle improvements in cleanliness, definition, background silence, low-end dynamics and imaging.

Whether it's worth the extra expense will depend on the rest of your system. I wouldn't consider it essential, but it is a meaningful upgrade for someone who has already invested in the Primo Plus and wants to squeeze a little more performance from it.
Conclusion

The Primo Plus is a very clever and well designed product.

Volumio has essentially taken the Preciso DAC and Rivo Plus streamer and squeezed them into one compact and considerably more affordable package. The result is an all-in-one solution that doesn't feel like a compromise.

The sound is exceptionally clean, neutral and transparent, with excellent resolution and imaging, but thankfully it doesn't cross the line into clinical or sterile territory. The NOS mode adds another, slightly more organic flavour and is a welcome addition.

I also like the overall philosophy of the product. Instead of wasting space and money on a giant touchscreen, Volumio has kept the chassis small and elegant and put the emphasis on the software experience and audio performance.

The Volumio OS is another major advantage. It is mature, intuitive and designed specifically around music playback, while the Primo Plus itself offers enough inputs, outputs and configuration options to cover most realistic use cases.

There are a few things I would change. The tiny display is functional rather than informative, and I would certainly like to see the input sampling rate displayed. There's no touchscreen or cover-art interface either, although I don't personally consider either a serious drawback. Spotify Lossless support is also still missing.

Nevertheless, at €1,199, I think the Primo Plus is one of the most convincing all-in-one streamer/DAC solutions I've encountered.

It gives you excellent DAC performance, a very capable streaming platform, extensive connectivity, adjustable preamp outputs, NOS functionality, a compact and elegant chassis and a very mature operating system, without the need to buy a separate streamer and DAC.
The review sample was kindly provided free of charge in exchange for an honest review. I don't use affiliate links.

The price of the Primo Plus is €1,199 and includes shipping, import duties and sales taxes, plus a lifetime subscription to Volumio Premium. It is available directly from 
Volumio
